draft.title: Globalisation
card: Globalisation is the growing links between countries. These links form through trade, investment, technology and the movement of people and ideas.
Trade
goods and services bought and sold across borders, such as phones made in one country and sold in another.
Investment
money sent between countries to buy shares, build businesses or lend funds, often within seconds by computer.
Technology
the internet, phones and faster transport link countries directly. They also help trade, investment, people and ideas move across borders.
draft.remember: Globalisation is the growing links between countries through trade, investment, technology and the movement of people and ideas.

a.q: Which example shows investment linking two countries?
opts: A Japanese company buys shares in an Australian mine
A Brazilian farm sells coffee beans to a German shop
A student from Kenya enrols at a Sydney university
A video from Korea is watched by viewers in Peru
a.why: Buying shares sends investment money from one country into a business in another. Selling coffee is trade, the student is a movement of people, and the video is a movement of ideas. The coffee is tempting because money is paid, but that is trade in a product.
a.clue: Which one puts money into a business in another country?

b.q: Hana in Perth sees a jacket on a video app. It was designed in Italy and sewn in Vietnam. She buys it online. What does this best show?
opts: Trade, technology and ideas link three countries in one sale
Only trade is involved, as she bought a product
The jacket is an investment between Italy and Vietnam
Globalisation only happens when people travel overseas
b.why: The jacket crossing borders is trade. The video app and online shop are technology, and the video also spreads ideas. So several links join the countries. Saying only trade is involved is tempting, but it ignores the technology and ideas.
b.clue: Look for the product, the app and the online shop.

a.best: A Japanese company buys shares in an Australian mine

b.best: Trade, technology and ideas link three countries in one sale

problems.detail: The card explains trade, investment and technology in their own bullets, but gives no bullet on the movement of people and ideas. Question a uses people and ideas as distractors, and question b's right answer depends on knowing that a video app spreads ideas, which the card never teaches.

check.summary: Both answers are clear and correct. The card leaves out any explanation of the movement of people and ideas, even though question b's answer, and question a's distractors, rely on it.
